title: Australian temperate reef fish thermal index followed 3-year SST at 0.35 C per C in 2008-2020 and again in 2021-2026, but only through region-wide year changes (549 sites)
abstract: We tested whether the reef fish thermal index (RFTI) on Australian temperate and subtropical reefs continued to follow sea surface temperature (SST) after the data window of Stuart-Smith et al. (2022). We used public Reef Life Survey and ATRC fish counts (CC BY 4.0) from 549 sites south of 25 S (5,344 site-years, 1992-2026) and NOAA OISST v2.1. We calculated a log-abundance-weighted RFTI from species thermal midpoints and compared each site with itself. Within sites, the RFTI increased by 0.35 C per 1 C of mean SST in the 36 months before the survey in 2008-2020 (95% CI 0.20 to 0.50) and by the same amount in the new period 2021-2026 (0.35, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.53). In 1992-2007 the slope was 0.16 (0.11 to 0.21). SST after the survey did not predict the RFTI. Survey visibility, depth, month, survey-month SST and program did not explain the slope. Resident species alone gave about 57% of it; transient species gave the rest. Cooling years decreased the RFTI at least as much as warm years increased it (no ratchet). The 2008-2020 slope reduced 2021-2026 prediction error by 7.0% relative to the site mean (95% CI -2.3% to 14.2%), because SST changed only 0.10 C between periods. Main limitation: the link came from region-wide warm and cool years. With region-year effects, local SST did not predict the RFTI (2008-2020: -0.01, 95% CI -0.20 to 0.18). Thus the data cannot separate SST from other region-wide year effects, for example larval supply or survey-team changes, because the public data do not identify divers.
